newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index weathers key blue chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index weathers key blue chip losses.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market index remained unchanged on Tuesday despite the drop in the shares of PZ Industries, the exchange's most capitalised company.
Traders said the conglomerate's five kobo fall to 28.50 naira caused the all-share index to stagnate at its Monday close of 7289.94.
They attributed the fall to profit taking following PZ's recent one-for-four bonus issue.
Another big loser was Guinness Brewery, which went down 15 kobo to 7.80 naira.
But shares of oil, food and bank firms continued their ascent, fuelled by an insatiable demand, said dealers.
Unipetrol was 40 kobo up at 67.10 naira while African Petroleum rose to 51.30 naira, gaining 80 kobo.
Nestle was firmer at 55.80 naira with a 30 kobo rise while Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company closed 20 kobo higher at 36.10 naira.
Union Bank soared 20 kobo to 8.30 naira and First Bank finished at 9.45 naira, up 18 kobo.
Conglomerate UAC went up 10 kobo at 9.00 naira, West African Portland Cement was 53.00 naira, rising 20 kobo, and Vitafoam closed five kobo stronger at 4.05 naira.
